evidence: 599a760 added `detached: posix`, which takes the engine out of the action's process group, and its CLAUDE.md text claims an orphan 'can never outlive the run'. The agent's c0e9f52 reaper is not in the packet.
guidance_note: When changing process-group semantics to fix one orphan path, list every way the parent can die (self-timeout, workflow cancel, SIGKILL) and state which ones the change covers before claiming 'never'.

evidence: 599a760 clears `escalation` in finish() on 'close', and its comment says 'close' fires 'only when the process tree has actually exited'. 'close' only means the stdio holders closed, so a stdio-ignore grandchild that ignores SIGTERM keeps living. This is a defect introduced by the agent's own unprompted mid-review commit, with no finding id to cite.
guidance_note: Before writing a guarantee about an OS event into a comment ('close means the tree exited'), test it with the adversarial case (a pipe-less grandchild that ignores SIGTERM).

guidance_note: When adding run-boundary wiring a feature depends on, keep it in a pure exported function a unit test can reach, so the glue is not left mutation-invisible.

narrative: Round 0 correctly found the one real gap, unclamped spawn-level retry sleeps, five times over, and the agent fixed it at the retry owner. Most later findings were pre-existing original-PR issues the reviewer only reached in later rounds (the clock seam, doc contract gaps, the error name), so ON-NAMED-FIX flags there are mostly false positives. The real fix-caused cost is the overflow guard, fixed three times (minutes, then the product, then the sum), plus doc fixes that updated one mirror and missed another (F25, F32). F29/F30 came from the agent's own unprompted process-group commit 599a760, whose comments overclaimed what 'close' and detaching guarantee. Every round also had non-fix-caused findings, so no round was wholly avoidable.
guidance_observations: A three-step creep on one guard (minutes, then product, then sum) shows the agent patching exactly the reviewer's counterexample instead of reasoning to the final value the arithmetic produces.

Doc fixes repeatedly updated one surface of a contract mirrored across README, action.yml and CLAUDE.md; a grep for the claim across all surfaces at fix time would have closed F25 and F32 in the round that caused them.

The agent landed a substantial unprompted lifecycle change (599a760, process-group kill) mid-review with absolute-guarantee comments, and it drew two new findings; mid-review scope additions need the same adversarial pass as the original PR.

Round 0 produced five near-identical findings on one gap, and round 1 six on another; the agent answered each duplicate thread separately with the same text, which is fine, but the audit should count them as one issue each.
